notes: Generic JTBD patterns synthesized across 70+ anonymized student venture submissions. Each card represents a job pattern shared by at least five teams in the dataset; no card maps to a single submission.

cards.persona: front-line clinician in a busy outpatient practice
cards.situation: the next patient is already in the room and the chart is half-finished
cards.want: a clean visit summary, screener results, and prior history surfaced in front of me without me typing it
cards.outcome: spend the visit looking at the patient instead of catching up on documentation later that night

cards.persona: small-practice owner running a clinic on thin margins
cards.situation: calls go unanswered, claims get denied, and shifts go unfilled while staff are stretched
cards.want: the routine intake, scheduling, follow-up, and billing fixes handled in the background so booked appointments actually happen
cards.outcome: stop leaking revenue at the front desk and keep the lights on without hiring people we cannot afford

cards.persona: patient living with a chronic or post-treatment condition
cards.situation: weeks pass between appointments and symptoms, side effects, and missed routines stack up
cards.want: someone keeping track of how I am actually doing day to day and nudging the right behavior before things slip
cards.outcome: stay on plan and avoid the next preventable hospital visit instead of only being seen when something breaks

cards.persona: family caregiver or care coordinator for an aging adult
cards.situation: an older relative is at home alone and small risks like a fall or a missed medication can become emergencies
cards.want: an unobtrusive set of eyes that flags concerning changes without putting cameras or wearables on my parent
cards.outcome: let them stay independent at home longer and respond fast when something is genuinely wrong

cards.persona: operations or maintenance lead at a mid-size plant or warehouse
cards.situation: a critical asset is showing early warning signs but the team only finds out after a costly stoppage
cards.want: the unusual pattern noticed and explained early so the right repair gets scheduled before production halts
cards.outcome: turn unplanned downtime into routine maintenance and stop bleeding revenue on emergency fixes

cards.persona: buyer or operator working through a fragmented physical supply chain
cards.situation: contracts, certifications, shipments, and quality records live in spreadsheets, emails, and phone calls
cards.want: one trustworthy view of where every lot, load, or batch is and whether it meets the spec a customer is paying for
cards.outcome: win premium contracts that demand provenance instead of getting cut for being unable to prove what we sold

cards.persona: field worker making weather- or condition-driven decisions outdoors
cards.situation: a planting, irrigation, dispatch, or repair call has to be made today with limited time and limited data
cards.want: a clear recommendation in plain language that fits the conditions on my piece of ground right now
cards.outcome: stop wasting inputs and losing time to bad timing on calls that used to depend on pure guesswork

cards.persona: founder or operator at a small services business
cards.situation: interest is coming in through calls, forms, and DMs faster than the team can answer
cards.want: every inbound lead greeted, qualified, and booked the moment it arrives, in our voice and our rules
cards.outcome: stop losing customers to whoever responds first and turn existing demand into actual appointments

cards.persona: knowledge worker juggling many tools, meetings, and follow-ups
cards.situation: the day is full of conversations and decisions that vanish the moment they end
cards.want: what was said, decided, and promised captured and brought back to me at the right moment without typing it up
cards.outcome: follow through on commitments and reclaim the hours that disappear into note-taking and re-explaining context

cards.persona: college student trying to keep up across many tools and courses
cards.situation: deadlines, materials, and study sessions are scattered across portals, PDFs, and group chats
cards.want: one calm place that tells me what is due, what to study next, and helps me actually learn it
cards.outcome: stop drowning in logistics and put the time into learning the material instead

cards.persona: campus staff member buried under routine inbound questions across financial aid, advising, and enrollment
cards.situation: the same routine questions arrive every day faster than a small team can answer them, while the students who genuinely need help wait
cards.want: the routine questions answered accurately and on the record so my time goes to the students who actually need a human
cards.outcome: give every student a faster answer and still have hours left for the conversations only I can have

cards.persona: person preparing for a real-life performance moment
cards.situation: an interview, presentation, difficult conversation, or physical performance is coming up and no one will give honest practice feedback
cards.want: a private space to rehearse, refine my delivery, and get specific feedback on how I came across or moved
cards.outcome: walk into the room with real confidence instead of hoping it goes well

cards.persona: consumer drowning in options and conflicting advice for everyday decisions
cards.situation: a routine choice such as what to buy, eat, or take has too many options and too much marketing noise
cards.want: a neutral recommendation that reflects who I am, not what someone is paid to push
cards.outcome: feel confident I picked the right thing for me and stop wasting time and money on bad guesses

cards.persona: resident in an under-resourced setting trying to reach a public service that exists on paper
cards.situation: a moment of need shows up faster than the small team or hotline behind the service can respond to it
cards.want: the right rule, route, or report delivered to whoever needs it now, even from a basic phone and without expert knowledge of the system
cards.outcome: make a public service that was theoretical actually reach the people it was built for

cards.persona: small-business owner or everyday consumer dealing with rules-heavy financial paperwork
cards.situation: a denial, dispute, or compliance form is in the way of money owed or a benefit that should already apply
cards.want: the next correct step explained and handled in plain language without paying an enterprise specialist
cards.outcome: actually collect what is mine and move on instead of giving up because the process is hostile
